You are sandy_walnut42, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll inspect the bundled docs and probe the executable’s main CLI paths first, then implement a baseline and compare outputs.

[![Continuous integration](https://github.com/tamasfe/taplo/workflows/Continuous%20integration/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tamasfe/taplo/actions?query=workflow%3A%22Continuous+integration%22) [![Latest Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/taplo.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/taplo) [![Documentation](https://docs.rs/taplo/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/taplo) [**Website**](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev) # Taplo This is the repository for Taplo, a TOML v1.0.0 toolkit, more details on the [website](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev). - [Taplo](#taplo) - [Status](#status) - [Contributing](#contributing) ## Status The project is very young, so bugs and incomplete features are expected, so [any help is welcome](CONTRIBUTING.md)! The correctness of the TOML parsing and decoding is not yet entirely guaranteed (as there is no official 1.0.0 compliance test suite yet). ## Contributing All kinds of contributions are welcome. Make sure to read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first! # Introduction Taplo CLI aims to be an one stop shop tool for working with TOML files via the command line. The features include validation, formatting, and querying TOML documents with a [jq](https://stedolan.github.io/jq/)-like fashion. # Formatting It is possible to format files in-place or via standard i/o. ```sh taplo fmt foo.toml ``` Or ```sh cat foo.toml | taplo fmt - ``` ::: info By default Taplo will bail on documents that contain syntax errors to avoid destructive edits, you can use the `--force` flag to suppress this and try to format the invalid document(s) anyway. ::: ## Options Formatter options are read from the [configuration file](./configuration.md#configuration-file), on top of that it is possible to specify overrides via the `--option` flag: ```sh taplo fmt --option indent_tables=false foo.toml ``` ## Check It is possible to check whether the given files are properly formatted via the `--check` flag. When this flag is supplied, no formatting will be done. # Conversion and Extraction Taplo makes it easy to convert TOML files to JSON and also extract specific values via the `get` command. ## Examples The following examples use the TOML file below: ```toml # foo.toml [foo] bar = true [[baz]] baz_field = "baz 1" [[baz]] baz_field = "baz 2" ``` ## Converting to JSON ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml -o json ``` This will yield the following output: ```json { "foo": { "bar": true }, "baz": [ { "baz_field": "baz 1" }, { "baz_field": "baz 2" } ] } ``` ## Extracting Specific Values It is possible to extract specific values via a simple query expressions. ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml 'baz[1].baz_field' ``` This will yield: ``` baz 2 ``` ::: warning Expressions with array patterns `[]` might need to be put between quotation marks for some shells. ::: ::: info List indexing is 0-based. ::: By default the value will be "parsed", so that no strings will contain escape sequences or quotation marks. However it is also possible to change the output format to JSON: ```sh taplo get -f foo.toml -o json baz ``` will yield: ```json [ { "baz_field": "baz 1" }, { "baz_field": "baz 2" } ] ``` ### More Examples More examples for query expressions using the same document above: | expression | output format | output | | :---------------: | :-----------: | :--------------------: | | `baz.0.baz_field` | json | `"baz 1"` | | `baz.*.baz_field` | json | `[ "baz 1", "baz 2" ]` | | `baz.1.baz_field` | value | `baz 2` | | `baz.1` | toml | `baz_field = "baz 2"` | ::: info The outputs have been slightly modified to fit into the table format. :::# Validation Taplo supports validation of TOML files, by default it will only look for syntax errors and some semantic errors such as duplicate keys. ```sh taplo check foo.toml ``` ## Schema Validation Taplo supports validation via [JSON Schemas](https://json-schema.org) (Draft 4). ### Using a Specific Schema ```sh taplo check --schema https://example.com/foo-schema.json foo.toml ``` ### Using a Schema Catalog Taplo supports schema catalogs such as the [JSON Schema Store](https://www.schemastore.org/json/) for retrieving schemas and matching them to files via file names. You can enable this by either specifying a catalog via the `--schema-catalog` flag, or enabling the use of the default catalogs via `--default-schema-catalogs`. "}}

Taplo uses the Rust `tracing` library for configurable logging features and respects the `RUST_LOG` environment variable. All logs regardless of log level are printed to the standard error output.

In most cases you might wish to disable logging below a certain log level.
As an example if you wish to only see error messages, you can do the following:

```sh
RUST_LOG=error taplo lint foo.toml
```

The available log levels:

- `trace`
- `debug`
- `info`
- `warn`
- `error`

Taplo supports validation of TOML files, by default it will only look for syntax errors and some semantic errors such as duplicate keys.

```sh
taplo check foo.toml
```

## Schema Validation

Taplo supports validation via [JSON Schemas](https://json-schema.org) (Draft 4).

### Using a Specific Schema

```sh
taplo check --schema https://example.com/foo-schema.json foo.toml
```

### Using a Schema Catalog

Taplo supports schema catalogs such as the [JSON Schema Store](https://www.schemastore.org/json/) for retrieving schemas and matching them to files via file names.

You can enable this by either specifying a catalog via the `--schema-catalog` flag, or enabling the use of the default catalogs via `--default-schema-catalogs`.

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/toml_parser.py
+"""Small TOML 1.0 value parser for Python versions before 3.11.
+
+It intentionally exposes the same simple ``loads`` interface as tomllib and
+uses only the Python standard library.
+"""
+import ast
+import datetime
+import json
+import re
+
+
+class TomlDecodeError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _split_top(s, sep=','):
+    out=[]; start=0; depth=0; quote=None; triple=False; esc=False; i=0
+    while i<len(s):
+        c=s[i]
+        if quote:
+            if quote=='"' and esc: esc=False
+            elif quote=='"' and c=='\\': esc=True
+            elif triple and s.startswith(quote*3,i): quote=None; triple=False; i+=2
+            elif not triple and c==quote: quote=None
+        elif c in "\"'":
+            quote=c; triple=s.startswith(c*3,i)
+            if triple: i+=2
+        elif c in '[{(': depth+=1
+        elif c in ']})': depth-=1
+        elif c==sep and depth==0: out.append(s[start:i].strip()); start=i+1
+        i+=1
+    out.append(s[start:].strip())
+    return out
+
+
+def _strip_comment(s):
+    parts=_split_top(s,'#')
+    return parts[0].rstrip()
+
+
+def _key(s):
+    s=s.strip()
+    if not s: raise TomlDecodeError('empty key')
+    if s[0] in "\"'":
+        try:
+            if s[0]=='"': return json.loads(s)
+            return s[1:-1]
+        except Exception as e: raise TomlDecodeError('invalid quoted key') from e
+    if not re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_-]+',s): raise TomlDecodeError('invalid bare key')
+    return s
+
+
+def _keys(s):
+    return [_key(x) for x in _split_top(s,'.')]
+
+
+def _value(s):
+    s=s.strip()
+    if not s: raise TomlDecodeError('expected value')
+    if s.startswith('"""') or s.startswith("'''"):
+        q=s[:3]
+        if len(s)<6 or not s.endswith(q): raise TomlDecodeError('unterminated multiline string')
+        body=s[3:-3]
+        if q=='"""':
+            body=body.replace('\\\n','').replace('\\\r\n','')
+            try: return json.loads('"'+body.replace('"','\\"')+'"')
+            except Exception: return body
+        return body
+    if s[0] in "\"'":
+        try: return json.loads(s) if s[0]=='"' else s[1:-1]
+        except Exception as e: raise TomlDecodeError('invalid string') from e
+    if s.startswith('['):
+        if not s.endswith(']'): raise TomlDecodeError('unterminated array')
+        body=s[1:-1].strip()
+        return [] if not body else [_value(x) for x in _split_top(body) if x]
+    if s.startswith('{'):
+        if not s.endswith('}'): raise TomlDecodeError('unterminated inline table')
+        result={}; body=s[1:-1].strip()
+        if not body:return result
+        for item in _split_top(body):
+            kv=_split_top(item,'=')
+            if len(kv)!=2: raise TomlDecodeError('invalid inline table entry')
+            ks=_keys(kv[0]); cur=result
+            for k in ks[:-1]: cur=cur.setdefault(k,{})
+            if ks[-1] in cur: raise TomlDecodeError('duplicate key')
+            cur[ks[-1]]=_value(kv[1])
+        return result
+    if s in ('true','false'): return s=='true'
+    normalized=s.replace('_','')
+    if re.fullmatch(r'[+-]?0x[0-9a-fA-F]+',normalized): return int(normalized,16)
+    if re.fullmatch(r'[+-]?0o[0-7]+',normalized): return int(normalized,8)
+    if re.fullmatch(r'[+-]?0b[01]+',normalized): return int(normalized,2)
+    if re.fullmatch(r'[+-]?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)',normalized): return int(normalized)
+    if re.fullmatch(r'[+-]?(?:(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)|[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?',normalized):
+        try: return float(normalized)
+        except ValueError: pass
+    try:
+        if re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d',s): return datetime.date.fromisoformat(s)
+        if re.fullmatch(r'\d\d:\d\d:\d\d(?:\.\d+)?',s): return datetime.time.fromisoformat(s)
+        if re.match(r'^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d[Tt ]',s): return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace('Z','+00:00').replace('z','+00:00'))
+    except ValueError: raise TomlDecodeError('invalid date/time')
+    if s in ('inf','+inf','-inf','nan','+nan','-nan'):
+        return float('-inf') if s=='-inf' else float('inf') if s in ('inf','+inf') else float('nan')
+    raise TomlDecodeError('invalid value')
+
+
+def _statements(text):
+    # Collect logical lines while inside arrays, inline tables, or multiline strings.
+    buf=''; depth=0; quote=None; triple=False; esc=False
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        line=line.rstrip('\r')
+        if not buf and not line.strip(): continue
+        buf += ('\n' if buf else '')+line
+        i=0
+        while i<len(line):
+            c=line[i]
+            if quote:
+                if quote=='"' and esc: esc=False
+                elif quote=='"' and c=='\\': esc=True
+                elif triple and line.startswith(quote*3,i): quote=None; triple=False; i+=2
+                elif not triple and c==quote: quote=None
+            elif c=='#': break
+            elif c in "\"'":
+                quote=c; triple=line.startswith(c*3,i)
+                if triple:i+=2
+            elif c in '[{':depth+=1
+            elif c in ']}':depth-=1
+            i+=1
+        if not quote and depth<=0:
+            clean=_strip_comment(buf).strip()
+            if clean: yield clean
+            buf=''; depth=0
+    if buf.strip():
+        clean=_strip_comment(buf).strip()
+        if clean: yield clean
+
+
+def loads(text):
+    root={}; current=root; explicit=set(); dotted=set()
+    for stmt in _statements(text):
+        if stmt.startswith('['):
+            array=stmt.startswith('[[')
+            close=']]' if array else ']'
+            if not stmt.endswith(close): raise TomlDecodeError('invalid table header')
+            path=_keys(stmt[2:-2] if array else stmt[1:-1]); cur=root
+            for k in path[:-1]:
+                val=cur.get(k)
+                if isinstance(val,list) and val and isinstance(val[-1],dict): val=val[-1]
+                if val is None: val={}; cur[k]=val
+                if not isinstance(val,dict): raise TomlDecodeError('table conflicts with value')
+                cur=val
+            last=path[-1]
+            if array:
+                seq=cur.setdefault(last,[])
+                if not isinstance(seq,list): raise TomlDecodeError('array table conflicts')
+                item={};seq.append(item);current=item
+            else:
+                val=cur.setdefault(last,{})
+                if not isinstance(val,dict): raise TomlDecodeError('table conflicts with value')
+                p=tuple(path)
+                if p in explicit: raise TomlDecodeError('duplicate table')
+                explicit.add(p); current=val
+            continue
+        eq=_split_top(stmt,'=')
+        if len(eq)<2: raise TomlDecodeError('expected equals sign')
+        # Rejoin in case equality occurs inside value (e.g. strings are already protected by split helper).
+        keypart=eq[0]; valuepart='='.join(eq[1:]); path=_keys(keypart); cur=current
+        for k in path[:-1]:
+            if k not in cur: cur[k]={}
+            if not isinstance(cur[k],dict): raise TomlDecodeError('conflicting key')
+            cur=cur[k]
+        k=path[-1]
+        if k in cur: raise TomlDecodeError('duplicate key')
+        cur[k]=_value(valuepart)
+    return root
*** End Patch";

  -V, --version          Print version

    "config": "config_cmd",

def main(argv=None):

    if not args or args[0] in ("-h", "--help"):
        print(ROOT_HELP, end="")
        return 0
    if args[0] in ("-V", "--version"):
        print(VERSION)
        return 0
    # Global switches can be placed before the command.
    while args and args[0] in ("--verbose", "--log-spans"):
        args.pop(0)
    if args and args[0] == "--colors":
        del args[:2]
    if not args:
        print(ROOT_HELP, end="")
        return 0
    token = args.pop(0)
    command = ALIASES.get(token, token)
    if command == "help":
        if not args:
            print(ROOT_HELP, end="")
            return 0
        command = ALIASES.get(args.pop(0), "help")
        args.insert(0, "--help")

        return 0
    if command == "toml-test":
        return toml_test()
    module_name = MODULES.get(command)
    if not module_name:
        print(ROOT_HELP, end="", file=sys.stderr)

    try:

        return int(module.run(args) or 0)
    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:

        return 0
    except Exception:

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/format_cmd.py
+"""TOML formatter fallback used by the command dispatcher."""
+import datetime
+import difflib
+import glob
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+
+from toml_parser import loads
+
+
+def _key(s):
+    return s if s and all(c.isalnum() or c in '_-' for c in s) and not s[0].isdigit() else json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)
+
+
+def _value(v, compact=False):
+    if isinstance(v, bool): return 'true' if v else 'false'
+    if isinstance(v, str): return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
+    if isinstance(v, (datetime.date, datetime.time, datetime.datetime)):
+        return v.isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z')
+    if isinstance(v, float):
+        if v != v:return 'nan'
+        if v==float('inf'):return 'inf'
+        if v==float('-inf'):return '-inf'
+        return repr(v)
+    if isinstance(v, (int,)): return str(v)
+    if isinstance(v, list):
+        inside=', '.join(_value(x, compact) for x in v)
+        if not compact: inside=' '+inside+' ' if inside else ''
+        return '['+inside+']'
+    if isinstance(v, dict):
+        inside=', '.join(_key(k)+' = '+_value(x, compact) for k,x in v.items())
+        if not compact: inside=' '+inside+' ' if inside else ''
+        return '{'+inside+'}'
+    return str(v)
+
+
+def _format(doc, opts):
+    compact_entries=opts.get('compact_entries',False)
+    compact_arrays=opts.get('compact_arrays',False)
+    compact_inline=opts.get('compact_inline_tables',False)
+    reorder=opts.get('reorder_keys',False)
+    eol='\r\n' if opts.get('crlf',False) else '\n'
+    lines=[]
+    def entries(table, prefix=()):
+        keys=list(table)
+        if reorder: keys.sort()
+        for k in keys:
+            v=table[k]
+            if isinstance(v,dict) or (isinstance(v,list) and v and all(isinstance(x,dict) for x in v)):
+                continue
+            sep='=' if compact_entries else ' = '
+            lines.append(_key(k)+sep+_value(v, compact_arrays or compact_inline))
+        subtables=[k for k,v in table.items() if isinstance(v,dict)]
+        arraytables=[k for k,v in table.items() if isinstance(v,list) and v and all(isinstance(x,dict) for x in v)]
+        for k in subtables:
+            child=table[k]
+            if lines and lines[-1]!='': lines.append('')
+            path=prefix+(k,)
+            lines.append('['+'.'.join(_key(p) for p in path)+']')
+            entries(child,path)
+        for k in arraytables:
+            for child in table[k]:
+                if lines and lines[-1]!='': lines.append('')
+                path=prefix+(k,)
+                lines.append('[['+'.'.join(_key(p) for p in path)+']]')
+                entries(child,path)
+    entries(doc)
+    out=eol.join(lines)
+    if opts.get('trailing_newline',True): out+=eol
+    return out
+
+
+def run(args):
+    options={}; paths=[]; check=False; diff=False; force=False; i=0; stdinpath='-'
+    while i<len(args):
+        a=args[i]
+        if a in ('--check',): check=True
+        elif a=='--diff': diff=True
+        elif a in ('-f','--force'): force=True
+        elif a=='--stdin-filepath' and i+1<len(args): i+=1; stdinpath=args[i]
+        elif a in ('-o','--option') and i+1<len(args):
+            i+=1
+            try:
+                k,v=args[i].split('=',1)
+                options[k.replace('-','_')]=v.lower()=='true' if v.lower() in ('true','false') else int(v) if v.isdigit() else v
+            except ValueError: pass
+        elif a.startswith('-') and a!='-': pass
+        else: paths.append(a)
+        i+=1
+    if paths==['-'] or (not paths and not sys.stdin.isatty()):
+        src=sys.stdin.read()
+        try: out=_format(loads(src),options)
+        except Exception as e:
+            if not force: return 1
+            out=src
+        sys.stdout.write(out); return 0
+    files=[]
+    for pattern in paths:
+        files.extend(glob.glob(pattern,recursive=True))
+    for path in files:
+        try:
+            with open(path,encoding='utf-8',newline='') as f: src=f.read()
+            try: out=_format(loads(src),options)
+            except Exception:
+                if not force: return 1
+                continue
+            if check:
+                if src!=out:return 1
+                continue
+            if diff:
+                sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(src.splitlines(True),out.splitlines(True),fromfile=path,tofile=path))
+            with open(path,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='') as f: f.write(out)
+        except OSError:
+            continue
+    return 0
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r)

import datetime

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

from toml_parser import InlineTable, _keys, loads

FORMAT_HELP = """Format TOML documents.

Files are modified in-place unless the input comes from the standard input, in which case the formatted result is printed to the standard output.

Usage: taplo format [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...
          Paths or glob patterns to TOML documents.
          
          If the only argument is "-", the standard input will be used.

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Path to the Taplo configuration file
          
          [env: TAPLO_CONFIG=]

      --colors <COLORS>
          [default: auto]

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Determine whether to colorize output automatically
          - always: Always colorize output
          - never:  Never colorize output

      --cache-path <CACHE_PATH>
          Set a cache path

      --verbose
          Enable a verbose logging format

      --log-spans
          Enable logging spans

      --no-auto-config
          Do not search for a configuration file

  -o, --option <OPTIONS>
          A formatter option given as a "key=value", can be set multiple times.
          
          The valid options and values are available here: https://taplo.tamasfe.dev/configuration/formatter-options.html

  -f, --force
          Ignore syntax errors and force formatting

      --check
          Dry-run and report any files that are not correctly formatted

      --diff
          Print the differences in patch formatting to `stdout`

      --stdin-filepath <STDIN_FILEPATH>
          A path to the file that the Taplo CLI will treat like stdin.
          
          This option does not change the file input source. This option should be used only when the source input arises from the stdin.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
"""


def _key(s):
    return s if s and all(c.isalnum() or c in '_-' for c in s) and not s[0].isdigit() else json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)


def _value(v, compact=False, compact_inline=False, width=80, indent='  ', level=0, expand=True, trailing=True):
    if isinstance(v, bool): return 'true' if v else 'false'
    if isinstance(v, str): return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
    if isinstance(v, (datetime.date, datetime.time, datetime.datetime)):
        return v.isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z')
    if isinstance(v, float):
        if v != v:return 'nan'
        if v==float('inf'):return 'inf'
        if v==float('-inf'):return '-inf'
        return repr(v)
    if isinstance(v, (int,)): return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, list):
        rendered=[_value(x, compact, compact_inline, width, indent, level+1, expand, trailing) for x in v]
        inline=', '.join(rendered)
        if expand and rendered and len(inline)+2 > width:
            inside='\n'.join(indent*(level+1)+item+(',' if trailing else '') for item in rendered)
            return '[\n'+inside+'\n'+indent*level+']'
        inside=inline
        if not compact: inside=' '+inside+' ' if inside else ''
        return '['+inside+']'
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        inside=', '.join(_key(k)+' = '+_value(x, compact, compact_inline, width, indent, level, expand, trailing) for k,x in v.items())
        if not compact_inline: inside=' '+inside+' ' if inside else ''
        return '{'+inside+'}'
    return str(v)


def _format(doc, opts):
    compact_entries=opts.get('compact_entries',False)
    compact_arrays=opts.get('compact_arrays',True)
    compact_inline=opts.get('compact_inline_tables',False)
    reorder=opts.get('reorder_keys',False)
    width=opts.get('column_width',80)
    indent=opts.get('indent_string','  ')
    expand=opts.get('array_auto_expand',True)
    trailing=opts.get('array_trailing_comma',True)
    eol='\r\n' if opts.get('crlf',False) else '\n'
    lines=[]
    def entries(table, prefix=()):
        keys=list(table)
        if reorder: keys.sort()
        for k in keys:
            v=table[k]
            if (isinstance(v,dict) and not isinstance(v,InlineTable)) or (isinstance(v,list) and v and all(isinstance(x,dict) and not isinstance(x,InlineTable) for x in v)):
                continue
            sep='=' if compact_entries else ' = '
            key_text=_key(k)+sep
            lines.append(key_text+_value(v, compact_arrays, compact_inline, max(1,width-len(key_text)), indent, 0, expand, trailing))

import datetime
import difflib
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

from toml_parser import InlineTable, MultilineArray, _keys, loads

FORMAT_HELP = """Format TOML documents.

Files are modified in-place unless the input comes from the standard input, in which case the formatted result is printed to the standard output.

Usage: taplo format [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...
          Paths or glob patterns to TOML documents.
          
          If the only argument is "-", the standard input will be used.

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Path to the Taplo configuration file
          
          [env: TAPLO_CONFIG=]

      --colors <COLORS>
          [default: auto]

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Determine whether to colorize output automatically
          - always: Always colorize output
          - never:  Never colorize output

      --cache-path <CACHE_PATH>
          Set a cache path

      --verbose
          Enable a verbose logging format

      --log-spans
          Enable logging spans

      --no-auto-config
          Do not search for a configuration file

  -o, --option <OPTIONS>
          A formatter option given as a "key=value", can be set multiple times.
          
          The valid options and values are available here: https://taplo.tamasfe.dev/configuration/formatter-options.html

  -f, --force
          Ignore syntax errors and force formatting

      --check
          Dry-run and report any files that are not correctly formatted

      --diff
          Print the differences in patch formatting to `stdout`

      --stdin-filepath <STDIN_FILEPATH>
          A path to the file that the Taplo CLI will treat like stdin.
          
          This option does not change the file input source. This option should be used only when the source input arises from the stdin.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
"""


def _key(s):
    return s if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_-]+', s) else json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)


def _value(v, compact=False, compact_inline=False, width=80, indent='  ', level=0, expand=True, trailing=True, collapse=True):
    if isinstance(v, bool): return 'true' if v else 'false'
    if isinstance(v, str): return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
    if isinstance(v, (datetime.date, datetime.time, datetime.datetime)):
        return v.isoformat().replace('+00:00','Z')
    if isinstance(v, float):
        if v != v:return 'nan'
        if v==float('inf'):return 'inf'
        if v==float('-inf'):return '-inf'
        return repr(v)
    if isinstance(v, (int,)): return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, list):
        rendered=[_value(x, compact, compact_inline, width, indent, level+1, expand, trailing, collapse) for x in v]
        inline=', '.join(rendered)
        if expand and rendered and (len(inline)+2 > width or isinstance(v,MultilineArray) and not collapse):
            inside='\n'.join(indent*(level+1)+item+(',' if trailing else '') for item in rendered)
            return '[\n'+inside+'\n'+indent*level+']'
        inside=inline
        if not compact: inside=' '+inside+' ' if inside else ''
        return '['+inside+']'
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        inside=', '.join(_key(k)+' = '+_value(x, compact, compact_inline, width, indent, level, expand, trailing, collapse) for k,x in v.items())
        if not compact_inline: inside=' '+inside+' ' if inside else ''
        return '{'+inside+'}'
    return str(v)


def _normalize(v, opts):
    if isinstance(v, InlineTable):
        pairs=[(k,_normalize(x,opts)) for k,x in v.items()]
        if opts.get('reorder_inline_tables',False): pairs.sort(key=lambda kv: kv[0])
        return InlineTable(pairs)
    if isinstance(v,dict): return {k:_normalize(x,opts) for k,x in v.items()}
    if isinstance(v,list):
        values=[_normalize(x,opts) for x in v]
        if opts.get('reorder_arrays',False) and all(not isinstance(x,(dict,list)) for x in values):
            values.sort(key=lambda x: _value(x))
        return MultilineArray(values) if isinstance(v,MultilineArray) else values
    return v


def _format(doc, opts):
    doc=_normalize(doc,opts)
    compact_entries=opts.get('compact_entries',False)
    compact_arrays=opts.get('compact_arrays',True)
    compact_inline=opts.get('compact_inline_tables',False)
    reorder=opts.get('reorder_keys',False)

    trailing=opts.get('array_trailing_comma',True)
    collapse=opts.get('array_auto_collapse',True)
    indent_entries=opts.get('indent_entries',False)
    indent_tables=opts.get('indent_tables',False)
    eol='\r\n' if opts.get('crlf',False) else '\n'

                table_indent=indent*len(prefix) if indent_tables and prefix else ''
                lines.append(table_indent+'['+'.'.join(_key(p) for p in path)+']')
                entries(value,path)
